segments.text: The toughest animal on Earth must be huge. Well, that's not exactly true. It's about half a millimeter long.
Meet the tardigrade, also called the water bear. Eight chubby legs, tiny claws, and a face like a vacuum cleaner.
When things get bad, it dries out, pulls in its legs, and curls into a little ball called a tun. Its body almost completely stops.
Here's the wild part. In that state, it can survive freezing close to absolute zero, heat above boiling, and radiation hundreds of times what would kill you.
In fact, in {2007,|two thousand seven,} scientists sent tardigrades into space with no protection at all. Some of them survived, and even had babies.
That's not all. Some dried tardigrades have come back to life after years. Just add a drop of water.
They live almost everywhere: deep oceans, mountain tops, and probably in the moss outside your door.
So the toughest animal on Earth isn't huge. It's tiny, and it's probably right next to you.
